To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a trinocular edge-based approach can be used to synthesize novel views of a 3D scene from three uncalibrated images of that scene, 2) the approach can be applied to a variety of applications, 3) the quality of the results is comparable with that of other methods that require dense correspondences and/or calibrated cameras, 4) the method is robust to occlusions, and 5) the approach is fast and can be applied to large images

1) a trinocular edge-based approach to image transfer can produce results of comparable quality as state-of-the-art dense methods, 2) the proposed approach is more efficient, robust and flexible, 3) it can be extended to handle occlusions and 4) it is more general and can also be applied to other image processing problems

(1) trinocular matching of edges is more robust than dense matching, (2) trinocular edge-based transfer is more accurate and faster than dense transfer and (3) trinocular transfer outperforms dense transfer in all cases, even if the latter uses the same number of matches as the former.

the problem of view synthesis, or image interpolation, from a triplet of images taken from different points of view of the same scene, which is of great interest for many applications.
